transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I guess… I’m here because I can’t really turn my mind off anymore. It starts with something small, like a client not getting back to me, and then pretty quickly I’m thinking I’ll lose the contract, fall behind on divorce payments, and… never get back into a real leadership role. It just keeps going.
Do you find that your worries are persistent and hard to control, even when you try to stop thinking about them?

Yeah. It’s… pretty hard to stop once it starts. Like I said, one thing happens, a client doesn’t answer, and my mind just runs with it—contract’s gone, money problems, my whole career slipping away. I try to push it aside, but it doesn’t really listen.
Have you noticed any physical symptoms, like restlessness, feeling tired, or muscle tension, when these worries come up?

Yeah… I guess so. I feel pretty wound up most of the day. My shoulders get tight, like I’m bracing for something, and I’ll catch myself pacing around or bouncing my leg during calls, even when nothing’s actually happening.
Do you have trouble sleeping because of these worries, like difficulty falling asleep or staying asleep?

Yeah… most nights, honestly. I’ll lie there going over things in my head, like how I answered in an interview, or I’ll wake up and check the clock at 2 or 3. Even if I technically slept enough, I don’t really feel rested. It feels like I was on call all night.
Do you find yourself worrying about a variety of things beyond work or finances, like your health, relationships, or other responsibilities?

Yeah… it’s not just work, exactly. My mind kind of jumps around — contract stuff, the mortgage, whether people in the Bethesda tech scene think I’m… I don’t know, damaged goods. Even something like a recruiter taking too long to email back can feel like it means everything’s closing down.
How long have you been experiencing these constant worries and physical symptoms like tension and trouble sleeping?
Since I was fired… so, about thirteen months ago. It’s been pretty constant since then. Even after I got some contract work, it didn’t really settle down.
